title: Deploy origin-classifier to attribute eval regressions (config vs model vs infra) and auto-prioritize replays
creator: Anika Patel
description: Build and deploy a lightweight origin-classifier service that ingests failing eval snapshots and attributes likely causes (config delta, model variant change, infra anomaly, tokenizer drift, prompt mutation). Use the classifier to drive automated replay prioritization and targeted prompt-level test generation so post-incident follow-ups focus on the most actionable failure modes.
background: Recent incidents exposed long feedback loops in identifying why eval scores dropped after rollouts. Engineers currently triage with manual diffing across model and config deltas; this is slow and often misses subtle infra or tokenizer sources. We need an automated, auditable way to attribute regressions to accelerate fixes and reduce customer-facing exposure.
proposed_solution: 1) Train a binary/multiclass origin-classifier that consumes metadata features (config diff fingerprint, model hash, quantization profile, kernel selection, latency/queued-depth anomalies, tokenization checksum, recent infra incident tags) plus simple embedding comparisons of failing examples. 2) Package as a stateless microservice hooked into the eval alert pipeline to annotate incidents in real-time. 3) Use classifier confidence to automatically prioritize replay jobs and generate focused prompt-level tests for the CI/eval harness. 4) Surface classifier output and uncertainty in the postmortem template and Console incident timeline.
success_metrics: median triage time for eval regressions reduced to <6h
% of regressions with confident origin attribution >75%
replay queue prioritization reduces time-to-fix for P1 regressions by 30%
acceptance_criteria: Service returns origin tag (config|model|infra|tokenizer|unknown) and confidence score for incoming eval snapshot
Classifier integrates with existing eval alerting webhook and annotates the incident in the ticket
Automated replay creation respects classifier priority and starts within 15 minutes for top-priority incidents
Generated prompt-level test cases are pushed to eval harness as a draft PR with failing examples and reproduction steps
tasks: Define feature set and training labels from historical incidents (PM/SE review)
Assemble training dataset from last 24 months of eval postmortems and incident logs
Prototype classifier (lightweight XGBoost / small transformer) and evaluate on held-out incidents
Implement service with HTTP webhook input + authenticated pull for snapshot store
Wire service output into replay scheduler and create priority rules
Auto-generate prompt-level tests and create draft eval PRs
Add Console UI annotation and history link in incident timeline
Run canary on non-critical eval alerts for 2 weeks then ramp
risks: historical labels are noisy leading to low classifier precision
classifier overfits to config signatures and misses infra anomalies
automated replays could overload test infra if priority rules are too aggressive
false attributions could mislead postmortem; require human override path
